findings: The English-taught Data Science and Society BSc at Campus Fryslân, Leeuwarden, is 180 EC across three years. The dated catalog contains twelve required 5 EC courses in the first year. In year two, six 5 EC courses and the 10 EC co-created field project form the 40 EC common sequence. One four-course 20 EC specialization is required. This example uses the first listed, AI and Society, while Cognitive Technology is a separately evidenced direction. The 30 EC minor in the first semester of year three is open to approved subjects, including optional study abroad. The final semester comprises a 15 EC thesis and three 5 EC courses in advanced programming, research design and human–machine interaction. The official prospectus heading swaps the research design and thesis credits. The dated catalog and the individual CFBDS34A15 and CFBDS21A05 records govern and total 15 EC and 5 EC respectively.

The published first-year blocks sequence introductory data and programming before statistics, databases and big data, with parallel social, rights and governance study. The second year places social and business applications, digital rights, visual rhetoric, sustainability and simulation before the semester-long field project and specialized work. AI Advanced Skills I and AI Ethics and Politics run in 2A, then AI Advanced Skills II and AI Regulation run in 2B. The description of AI Advanced Skills II builds explicitly on Skills I. The reviewed individual 2026–27 course records state programme admission or contain no additional published prerequisite fields, including the field project, research design and thesis. The thesis runs across the final semester with Advanced Programming and Research Design in 2A and Human Machine Interaction in 2B. The research-design course prepares students to formulate a topic and methodological design for that final research. The optional UCR comparison element is outside the scheduled degree.

The closest response integrates programming, SQL databases, data visualization, machine learning and AI with statistics, social inquiry, digital strategy, rights and ethics. The added description-only Database Management Systems course teaches relational theory and SQL and is a stronger partner for the external databases course than networking. Human Rights: Law and Philosophy supplies general rights theory and protections, while the Groningen rights sequence applies them specifically to digital contexts. Sociology, ethics and governance are complementary across separate courses. Market Research and Strategy and Digital Transformation apply evidence and business decisions in settings distinct from the main technical sequence. Introductory Brain and Behavior precedes the available first-year Psycholinguistics offering. Later programming and data foundations support advanced image processing and deep learning. Both UCR plans differ substantively and exceed the four-course floor. The business-data and data-communication interests have curricular coverage inside the closest option and do not establish an additional distinct stable direction.
